lines: +# OE-STEP optimization notes
+## Baseline (stock, `bench --save-ref`, dev set)
+- boot 637.9 s; warm-up step 754.16 s; **timed step 663.27 s = rollout 430.24 + train+sync 233.03**
+- Trainer timers (timed step): ref_log_probs 33.0 s, log_probs 34.0 s, actor_train 142.6 s,
+  train total 210.6 s, weight sync ~3.2 s, sleep ~7.6 s.
+- Rollout-vs-trainer logprob mismatch (ref): mean_abs 0.0433, p99 0.461 → bench caps = 1.5×
+## Changes (all numerics-preserving)
+1. **Delta routed-experts (R3) transfer** (Miles `utils/http_utils.py`,
+   `rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py`).
+   Stock: every turn re-sends routed experts for the whole growing context
+   (42.6M token-rows ≈ 43 GB base64 per step; gather runs on the SGLang scheduler).
+   Now `post()` tags multi-turn sessions (episode id in `custom_params`), sends
+   `routed_experts_start_len` = rows already held, and the client stitches the delta onto
+   the accumulated array, returning the identical full array. Unit test:
+   `tests/fast/rollout/test_delta_routed_experts.py`.
+2. **Skip zero-coefficient ref-model forward** (Miles `backends/megatron_utils/actor.py`,
+   `backends/training_utils/loss/hub/losses.py`).
+   Baseline runs `--use-kl-loss --kl-loss-coef 0.00` and `kl_coef` defaults to 0, so the ref
+   log-probs are computed every step but multiplied by zero in both advantages and loss.
+   Skipped only when both coefficients are exactly 0 (loss hub mirrors the condition).
+3. **`--skip-actor-forward-only`** (launch) + dump capture (Miles `loss/hub/losses.py`,
+   `backends/megatron_utils/actor.py`, `utils/arguments.py`).
+   One on-policy optimizer step per rollout, so the training forward's detached log-probs
+   are exactly the old-policy log-probs; the separate 35 s forward-only pass is redundant.
+   The policy-loss hub captures those per-microbatch log-probs; the actor reassembles them
+   into `rollout_data["log_probs"]` before the debug dump. Verified bit-identical to the
+   forward-only pass on the dev step (mean/p99/max diff = 0.0 over 1.59M rows; rollout-vs
+   -trainer mismatch unchanged). Removed the stock validation entry that (only because the
+   dump lacked log-probs) declared it incompatible with `--save-debug-train-data`.
+   Unit test: `tests/fast/backends/test_skip_forward_logprob_assembly.py`.
+## Measured (bench, dev set, timed step)
+| config | step | rollout | train+sync | speedup | gates |
+| +skip-forward | TBD | | | | |
+## Tried and rejected (standalone 1-engine harness on dev episodes, 8-turn subset unless noted)
+- No speculative decoding 66.8 s vs EAGLE s2/d3/k1 49.0 s; s3/d4 50.7; s4/d5 54.5; tree
+  (s2/k4/d8, s3/k2/d8) 54–56 → stock spec config kept.
+- NGRAM speculative: 71.2 s and returned all-zero routed experts → unusable.
+- TP2 engines: per-GPU throughput dropped (1039 tok/s per 2-GPU engine vs 720/GPU at TP1).
+- DP-attention + DeepEP EP4 (FP8): 81 s for the full 64-episode subset vs ~49 s-equivalent
+  for 4×TP1; BF16 DeepEP only supports low_latency (fails on prefill sizes).
+- FlashInfer attention 48.8 vs FA3 49.0; mixed-chunk 49.6; spec-attention decode 48.8;
+  fused-qk-norm-rope 48.7 → all noise-level, not adopted.
+- MoE runner backends flashinfer_cutlass 50.0 / cutlass 48.8 vs triton 49.0 → kept auto.
+  (flashinfer_trtllm_routed, triton_kernel fail to start on this arch.)
+- Full FP8 rollout: 328.9 s vs 430 s BF16 for the heaviest engine's 16 episodes (full),
+  but FP8-vs-trainer logprob mean_abs 0.0732 / p99 0.730 exceeds caps 0.0650 / 0.691 → rejected.
+- FP8 KV cache: 355 s (7× slower; MLA FP8-KV fallback path) → rejected.
+- Trainer (train-only runs on captured rollout data): alltoall dispatcher identical
+  (Miles already rewrites allgather→alltoall for varlen); selective recompute OOM at
+  32768 tokens/microbatch; TP1+PP4 OOM on last-stage logits; TP2+PP2 needs EP≤2 (untried
+  further); 47 layers not divisible by PP without decoder-first/last layer counts.
+- Micro-batch layout was left untouched everywhere (max_tokens_per_gpu, DP1) because the
+  MTP auxiliary loss is normalized per micro-batch.
